title: SLO activation field kit & rolling ops playlist (30/60/90)
content:
Purpose:
This is a field-kit style playbook for a rolling 30/60/90 SLO activation pilot that pairs SRE, product, platform, and feature teams. It is intended to be a lightweight working guide for running an activation pilot (small number of services) and then scaling the patterns to the broader platform.

Background & context:
- We have many existing SLO playbooks but operations vary by team; this experiment standardizes a rolling ops playlist to accelerate adoption without heavy upfront process.
- Pilot goals: reduce incident-to-slo feedback time, validate monitoring signals for token-latency SLOs, and exercise cross-team escalations.
- Scope: 3 feature services (chat-api, embeddings-cache, batch-ingest) for a 90-day pilot.

High-level success metrics (end of 90 days):
- Adoption: 3 pilot services have production SLOs defined and onboarded to the SLO dashboard.
- Observability: alerts firing with <5% false-positive rate on primary SLO signals.
- Ops readiness: on-call runbook and escalation matrix validated with 2 tabletop runs.
- Regression detection: at least one quality regression detected by the SLO-eval hookup and triaged.

Primary risks & mitigations:
- Signal mismatch (metric doesn't reflect user experience): pair product PM + SRE to define golden query; run shadow-alerts for 2 weeks before enabling actioning.
- Alert storm when enabling new SLOs: use staged alerting (silent -> notify Slack channel -> page).
- Ownership confusion across platform boundaries: enforce the stakeholder pledge (see below) and require explicit handoff in the kickoff doc.

30/60/90 playbook (rolling ops playlist)
- Day 0 (pre-kickoff):
  - Identify service champion (engineer) and product owner.
  - Collect existing dashboards, paging rules, config repos.
  - Create pilot folder: linked artifacts + kickoff ticket (template in linked_artifacts).
  - Pre-checks: keys present in SLO schema, telemetry volume > 200 QPS for latency SLOs, span sampling enabled for distributed traces.

- 0-30 days (Discover & Define):
  - Week 1: kickoff meeting (roles: SRE lead, PM, service champion, platform eng rep). Outputs: target SLO (e.g., p99 < 220ms for generate-token), error budget policy, and the rollout window.
  - Week 2: define and validate signal queries. Run shadow-alerts (no pages) and collect false-positive/false-negative notes.
  - Week 3: finalize SLO config in the repo, open PR to add SLO to dashboard and automated reporting.
  - Week 4: tabletop walkthrough of runbook + simulated incident drill (paper exercise).

- 31-60 days (Enable & Observe):
  - Stage 1 enable: enable notify-only alerts to a pilot Slack channel (ops-slo-pilot). Monitor for noise for 7-10 days.
  - Signal refinement: adjust thresholds, add smoothing or rate-limiting if alerts spike.
  - Run 1 live incident triage if any real incidents occur; capture decision logs.
  - Monthly check-in with product & platform leadership; update exec one-pager.

- 61-90 days (Act & Scale):
  - If noise under control, promote alerts to paging with escalation policy.
  - Run a second tabletop that includes support + security + infra.
  - Postmortem any incidents and create action items (assign to owners).
  - Document lessons learned and create onboarding checklist for next wave.
  - Decide go/no-go to expand to 6 more services next quarter.

Weekly rituals during pilot:
- Pilot standup (30m) — Mon, owners review signals, open action items, and blocker list. Attendees: SRE lead, service champion, PM, platform rep.
- Ops health snapshot (auto email) — Thu morning: SLO burn rate, recent alerts, error budget usage.
- Retro + experiment notes — End of each 30d window; collect qualitative feedback from stakeholders.

Owners & roles (template):
- Pilot Lead (SRE): coordinates the playlist and chairs standups.
- Service Champion (Eng): implements SLO queries, runbooks, and PRs.
- Product Owner (PM): validates SLO aligns with product SLAs and customer impact.
- Platform Rep: ensures telemetry availability and validates resource quotas.
- On-call Lead: owns paging thresholds and escalation behavior.

Deliverables (per service):
- SLO definition PR merged (repo link)
- Runbook with triage steps and playbook for the top 3 failure modes
- Alerting staged config (silent -> notify -> page)
- Post-activation incident table and decision log
- Stakeholder pledge signed (recorded in kickoff doc)

Stakeholder pledge (copy into kickoff doc)
- "We, the undersigned, agree to the SLO target, error budget policy, and the staged alerting plan. Each signatory commits to timely response for escalations during the pilot and to participating in the 30/60/90 retros."
- Signatories required: Service Champion, SRE Lead, PM, Platform Lead, Customer Success (if customer-facing).

Runbook & escalation quick-reference (one-paragraph snippets for deck)
- If SLO burn rate > 2x for 15m -> notify pilot Slack channel (no page).
- If burn rate > 5x for 1h or customer-impacting errors spike -> page SRE on-call and trigger incident bridge.
- If SLO breach sustained for 6h -> escalate to platform eng manager and product lead; consider throttling non-essential workloads.

Experimentation & data collection plan:
- Collect per-minute SLI samples, tag by deployment SHA and region.
- Capture incident timelines and remediation steps for qualitative coding.
- Run A/B of two alert smoothing configs on embeddings-cache service to quantify noise reduction.

Communication templates
- Slack announcement template (used when moving from shadow -> notify): short summary + link to dashboard + expected user impact + contact.
- Exec 1-pager template: pilot objective, topline metrics, risks, recommended next step.

Open questions / decision log (working):
- Do we require product sign-off for all SLOs touching paid customers? (decision owner: PM Guild)
- Should silent-shadow mode run for a minimum of 14d for low-traffic services? (owner: Platform Eng)
- Rate-limiting policy for noisy metrics (histogram smoothing vs percentile rolling)? (owner: SRE Research)

Appendix: checklists (copyable)
- Kickoff checklist:
  - Confirm telemetry tags present (service, region, deployment_sha)
  - Create pilot ticket and link PR template
  - Add runbook skeleton to repo
  - Send stakeholder pledge for signatures

- Pre-promote checklist:
  - Shadow alerts run >= 7 days with <10% false positives
  - Runbook updated with simulation notes
  - On-call rota updated with escalation contacts

Notes to self (informal, keep at bottom):
- Keep playbook light; resistance grows with >6 mandatory steps.
- Expect engineering teams to push back on paging thresholds — bake in an automated rollback if churn hits 3 consecutive days.
- Coordinate with the billing/finance signal owners for any SLOs that affect cost-visible metrics.

Links & references (repeat for convenience):
- Pilot ticket template: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/OPS-301/rolling-ops-playlist-kickoff
- SLO schema & repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slo-configs
- Confluence starter page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Activation+Overview

Action items (next steps, owners)
- Priya: finalize kickoff deck + schedule initial kickoff by 2026-03-19.
- Jamal: create PR skeleton and repo folder for pilot services by 2026-03-16.
- Evelyn: route stakeholder pledge to PMs and collect signatures by 2026-03-20.
- Marcus: prepare shadow alert channel and metrics queries by 2026-03-18.

End of doc.
